steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a 9x13-inch baking dish with aluminum foil; set aside.
Combine carrots, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a resealable plastic bag and seal well; alternatively, use the carrot bag. Toss to coat evenly. Pour carrots into the prepared baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until tender, about 30 minutes. Sprinkle balsamic vinegar over carrots; shake the dish to coat evenly. Return to the oven and continue baking until liquid is absorbed, 5 to 10 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Balsamic Roasted Carrots
raw_recipe.description: These balsamic roasted carrots with olive oil, salt, and pepper are cooked in the oven, then seasoned with balsamic vinegar for a simple, delicious side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Balsamic Roasted Carrots

review.reviewBody: This was a great carrot recipe - I used whole carrots, chopped into pieces (into three lengthwise, and each into quarter lengths), and roasted them for much less time than indicated. They were in the oven at 425 degrees for 10 minutes, I added the balsamic and let cook 4 minutes more.

I'm not usually a big fan of cooked carrots but this recipe changed my mind. It's super easy to prepare, healthy, and delicious! The roasting time called for in the recipe is too long. (The first time I made these they burned). Instead I roasted for 15 minutes, then added the balsamic and roasted 10 minutes more. Perfection!

I needed to use my bag of whole carrots before we left town. I washed and cut them into 3-5 inch pieces. Tossed with the oil, sprinkled with garlic herb mix and baked, tossed with the balsamic vinegar. Perfect! We loved it!
Fabulous! I used toasted sesame oil, and a special spice blend; just a bit. I used whole assorted size and color heirloom carrots from my farm CSA.

Easiness rating is a 5. I used whole carrots that I cut into large pieces. Then I used the same bag that the carrots came in to toss them in vinegar and oil. I don't like single use plastic, but this made coating the carrots and clean up extra easy.

Really like these. I used regular carrots cut to a similar size, if not larger than baby carrots. I stirred them about halfway and cook a little less. They had a nice firmness to them which was nice. Will make again.

I hodgepodged it a bit - dried the baby carrots first as they are always stupid moist from the store, added red potatoes as they were starting to grow, and doubled the non-carrot ingredients accordingly. Added honey with the balsamic, came out great

While I could not taste this dish due to a stuffy nose, I tried this recipe for dinner with my parents and they really enjoyed it. I did, however, add thinly sliced white onions and baked the carrots/onion/vinegar mix for almost an hour as I enjoy softer carrots, periodically adding water so as not to burn. A simple dish and such a hit.

This was a great way to change up carrots without adding unnecessary ingredients. I used a high quality oil & honey balsamic vinegar with sea salt and fresh ground black pepper. I didn't follow exact measurements. I drizzled the oil and vinegar over the carrots and sprinkled with salt & pepper. I kept turning the carrots to keep the moist. This recipe was so easy and full of flavor. They turned out like candied carrots. Definitely a keeper!

We really enjoyed this dish. I oven bake carrots pretty regularly, but never thought to add balsamic vinegar. For 8 oz of carrots, I used only 1 Tbsp of vinegar, and we liked it a lot. Thanks for this easy way to change up a favorite veggie!

I made this recipe using only carrots as the vegetable because I wanted to use them while they were fresh. They were delicious. Normally my husband doesn't care for roasted vegetables, but even he complimented the taste without being asked for an opinion. The only other thing I changed was to add a teaspoon of melted butter to the marinade.
I love carrots in almost any form. My husband does not. I made this recipe because he is a fan of balsamic vinegar and he asked for thirds!
Loved it ! Made it use 1/2 carrots & 1/2 parsnips. I like that no sugar except what's in the balsamic vinegar was added

I made this dish for my father and I, for Thanksgiving dinner and it delivered!!! It was both tangy and sweet!!! I had to adjust the cooking time as my father only had regular bagged carrots, not baby carrots. Plus next time that I make them, I would use more balsamic vinegar, as I love it!!!
I added a little onion powder and a pinch of dry mustard.
This was easy and delicious. Used quartered carrots and cooked 25 minutes total.
These carrots were delicious.!!! I might have added a tad more balsamic vinegar than called for. We will be having these again and soon.
Made these for our family Christmas Eve gathering and everyone loved them. The recipe is so easy and delicious! Definitely putting this in my favorites.
So easy and quick to make. Tastes delicious. A wonderful dish.

I did make changes, and yes I will definitely make these again!!! I'm not one to measure too much when I cook... only when I bake.. so I don't even know how much EVOO, salt or pepper I used.. but I also added paprika, dill, and parsley flakes.. These carrots were awesome and I can't wait to make them again!
